projective_trans_image_size — 2D geometry op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "projective_trans_image_size", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: projective_trans_image_size (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

Sweeping knob a (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ projective_trans_image_size: knob a sweep (docs site)

Sweeping knob b (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ projective_trans_image_size: knob b sweep (docs site)

On other images (synthetic scene / photo / coins. Top row: inputs, bottom row: their outputs. Knobs at default):

▸ projective_trans_image_size: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

The implementation is identical to `projective_trans_image (kind: "projective"). The name implies the output size can be specified, but this backend does not change the output canvas size and returns exactly the same trapezoidal distortion as projective_trans_image (a limitation of the approximation — the size-change feature is not reproduced). A stand-in for HALCON's projective_trans_image_size` (Apply a projective transformation to an image and specify the output image size.).
